lines.text: When a bus pulls away, you lean back. Robots do too. Our robot's weight sits about twenty centimeters up.
Speed up, and weight slides to the back wheels. At six meters per second squared, each front wheel carries seventy-six newtons. Each back wheel, two hundred eighteen.
But all four motors push the same. The light front wheels slip first, while the heavy back wheels still have grip to spare.
Push to ten, and the front wheels carry almost nothing.
A low current limit would choke the back wheels too, right when they could help. So we keep the limit high, and plan the push with physics.
